name: MyLife Door Sensor
description: A wireless, battery-powered open/close sensor sold in a kit, which mounts on a door and reports when it opens or closes.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Remove the sensor cover by prying up at "open".
Install the included AA battery; don't replace the cover yet.

Peel the backing off the tape on the sensor and press it onto the door or window frame, with the SET button between the door or window edge and the battery (about 3 inches from the top on a door), so the door or window just clears it.
Press and hold the sensor's SET button for 5 seconds, until the LED starts blinking.

In the US, press and hold the SET button on the nearest Range Extender (formerly Access Point) until it beeps. If the sensor's LED keeps blinking, it is out of range: move the Range Extender closer and try again.
Peel the backing off the magnet's tape and mount the magnet within 1/2 inch of the sensor, lined up with the arrows on the sensor.
Test by opening and closing the door or window.
steps.expect: LED blinks once on each open and close

notes: The sensor is closed when the magnet is within 1/2 inch and open when it is farther.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.

notes: Then turn the responder on (or set it to any state) and press and hold its SET button for 3 seconds; the sensor's LED turns solid green. By default the sensor turns responders on when it opens and off when it closes.
When adding it to a Hub, press and hold the SET button until the LED blinks and then tap the SET button (the LED double-blinks).
The sensor is a controller only.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Tap the SET button.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping a few times to check the link.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds to finish.

notes: The device must already be in linking mode when the Hub starts ALL-Linking, since the Hub waits only about 10 seconds. This links the device's group 1 to the Hub; the Hub makes no link to the device.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, set it to the scene state and press and hold its SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds to finish.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again for 3 seconds.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds; the sensor's LED stops blinking and turns solid.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: While the sensor is awake, send the Stay Awake command (extended, cmd1 0x2E, cmd2 0x00, data 2 0x04, data 3 the number of seconds to stay awake).

notes: The sensor sleeps quickly to save battery and must be awake to send or receive messages; 0xF0 seconds is about 4 minutes, and the maximum is 0xFF.
How to wake the sensor before sending the command isn't known.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Unlink any responders from the sensor.
Gently remove the sensor's case with a small screwdriver.
Remove the battery.
Wait at least 15 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button while reinstalling the battery.
Release the SET button when the status LED turns on.
steps.expect: LED stays on about 4 seconds, then turns off

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Remove the sensor as a controller from each of its responders.

verification.note: Read from the Open/Close Sensor 2843, which shares its device category; no document describes this sensor.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene on the Hub first.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again for 3 seconds.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking for group 0, so it answers as the responder; the device deletes its link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: If the LED is still blinking, tap the SET button until it stops.

notes: The Hub won't remove a device that still belongs to a scene.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

notes: Its heartbeat's cmd1 is 0x11 while it's open and 0x13 while it's closed.

verification.note: An open/close sensor sold in a kit, read from its device category: it shares category 0x10 with the Open/Close Sensor 2843, and its commands, groups and setup are read from that sensor. The HouseLinc device catalog lists subcategory 0x09 as the Door Sensor 2843-232; no other document gives its model number, and none describes the sensor itself.
